title: Diversifying from vanaspati into IT
statement: Premji inherited a cooking-oil business at 21 after his father's death and pivoted the family enterprise into the nascent IT industry when he saw hardware and later software services as the growth frontier.
outcome: WIPRO became one of India's great IT services firms; the pivot from hydrogenated vegetable oil to technology is the founding legend of Indian business diversification.

title: The 1999 NYSE listing
statement: Premji listed Wipro on the New York Stock Exchange as part of the first wave of Indian technology ADRs, accessing global capital and credibility.
outcome: The listing, alongside Infosys's NASDAQ listing the same year, marked Indian IT's arrival as a global institutional investment class.

title: Azim Premji Foundation — pledging most of his wealth to education
statement: Premji transferred billions of dollars of Wipro stock into his foundation, focusing on public primary education in India rather than elite institutions.
outcome: The foundation became one of the world's largest private funders of education research and systems reform; Premji ultimately gave away more of his net worth proportionally than almost any living billionaire and signed the Giving Pledge.

title: Resisting the 2000-2001 rush to fire and rehire cheap staff
statement: During the IT downturn, Premji declined to mass-retrench while competitors fired and rehired at lower wages, absorbing the margin hit.
outcome: Wipro's retention record became a durability advantage in talent markets and a core element of Premji's reputation for frugal, long-horizon stewardship.
